questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of Organising' refers to.
questions.a: The managerial process that puts plans into motion by spelling out jobs and working relationships and by deploying people and resources so that the intended results are actually achieved.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of Organising'.
questions.a: It coordinates human effort, gathers resources and welds the two into one working whole for the stated objectives.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning of Organising' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.1 (source: lebs105.txt lines 150-187 (Meaning; school fete example; definitions by Louis Allen and Theo Haimann))

concepts.title: Steps in the Process of Organising

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Steps in the Process of Organising' refers to.
questions.a: Four ordered steps: split the total work into manageable activities, group similar activities into departments, hand each post its duties matched to the person's competence, and settle who reports to whom by fixing authority relationships.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Steps in the Process of Organising'.
questions.a: Departmentalisation can rest on territory or product; the last step builds the hierarchy that later channels coordination.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Steps in the Process of Organising' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.1 (source: lebs105.txt lines 188-309 (Steps i to iv: division of work, departmentalisation, assignment of duties, reporting relationships))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Importance of Organising' refers to.
questions.a: The payoffs of doing the function well: routine tasks build worker specialisation, reporting lines become unambiguous, resources stop being duplicated, the structure can bend with the environment, administration runs clearly, people grow through delegation, and the firm gains room to expand and diversify.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Importance of Organising'.
questions.a: Seven benefits -- specialisation, clarity in working relationships, optimum resource use, adaptation to change, effective administration, development of personnel, expansion and growth.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Importance of Organising' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.2 (source: lebs105.txt lines 310-475 (Importance i to vii))

concepts.title: Organisation Structure and Span of Management

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Organisation Structure and Span of Management' refers to.
questions.a: The frame inside which a firm's managerial and operating tasks are carried out, mapping the relationships among people, work and resources; the span of management -- how many subordinates one superior can effectively supervise -- decides how many levels the structure will carry.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Organisation Structure and Span of Management'.
questions.a: As firms grow, coordination needs a reviewed structure; a wrong structure, Drucker warns, can wreck performance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Organisation Structure and Span of Management' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.1 (source: lebs105.txt lines 476-584 (Organisation Structure; span of management; travel agency example))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Functional Structure' refers to.
questions.a: A design that groups jobs of a similar nature into separate departments such as production, purchase, marketing, accounts and personnel, all reporting to one coordinating head.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Functional Structure'.
questions.a: Strengths: specialisation, easy training, minimal duplication and economies of scale. Weaknesses: functional empires, inter-department conflict and narrow outlook; it suits large firms needing deep specialisation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Functional Structure' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.2 (source: lebs105.txt lines 595-722 (Functional structure, advantages a-f, disadvantages a-d, suitability))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Divisional Structure' refers to.
questions.a: A design built from separate self-contained business units, one per product line or market, each headed by a divisional manager who owns the unit's performance and runs its own production, marketing and finance functions as a profit centre.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Divisional Structure'.
questions.a: Merits: product specialisation, accountability for profits, faster decisions, easy expansion. Demerits: inter-division conflict over funds, costly duplication of functions, powerful heads; it suits multi-product enterprises.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Divisional Structure' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.3 (source: lebs105.txt lines 723-902 (Divisional structure, advantages a-d, disadvantages a-c, suitability, comparison table))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Formal Organisation' refers to.
questions.a: The deliberately designed structure of authority and responsibility that management creates to get its plans carried out, with clear boundaries of who reports to whom and rules that guide conduct.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Formal Organisation'.
questions.a: It puts work above personal ties, keeps unity of command and stability, but can breed procedural delays and stiffle creativity; its structure may be functional or divisional.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Formal Organisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4.1 (source: lebs105.txt lines 1078-1238 (Formal organisation: meaning, features a-e, advantages, limitations))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Informal Organisation' refers to.
questions.a: The web of personal and social relationships that springs up by itself when colleagues interact beyond their official roles -- lunch groups, cricket circles, gossip networks -- with no written rules and no fixed direction of communication.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Informal Organisation'.
questions.a: It arises from within the formal structure, obeys group norms rather than rules, and can speed information and satisfy social needs -- or spread rumours and resist change; management is advised to work with it, not against it.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Informal Organisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4.2 (source: lebs105.txt lines 1239-1423 (Informal organisation: meaning, features a-e, comparison, advantages, disadvantages))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Delegation and Its Three Elements' refers to.
questions.a: The downward handover of authority by a superior to his subordinate, resting on three elements: authority, the right to command and decide; responsibility, the duty to perform the assigned task; and accountability, answerability for the final outcome, which can never be passed on.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Delegation and Its Three Elements'.
questions.a: Authority is delegated, responsibility is assumed, accountability is imposed -- authority flows down, responsibility and accountability flow up; delegation is never abdication.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Delegation and Its Three Elements' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 5.1 (source: lebs105.txt lines 1424-1639 (Delegation; elements: authority, responsibility, accountability; overview table))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Importance of Delegation' refers to.
questions.a: Why handing authority down pays: managers escape routine work and manage better, subordinates grow into future leaders, employees feel trusted and motivated, expansion gets a ready cadre, the hierarchy itself stands on delegated authority, and duties stop overlapping.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Importance of Delegation'.
questions.a: Six benefits -- effective management, employee development, motivation, facilitation of growth, basis of management hierarchy, better coordination.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Importance of Delegation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 5.1 (source: lebs105.txt lines 1640-1743 (Importance of Delegation i to vi))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Decentralisation and Its Importance' refers to.
questions.a: The systematic spread of decision-making authority to every level of the organisation, placing decisions nearest the action; it treats dispersal of authority as a philosophy of trust in people's competence rather than a mere handover of tasks.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Decentralisation and Its Importance'.
questions.a: Six benefits -- initiative among subordinates, managerial talent for the future, quicker decisions, relief to top management, facilitation of growth, better control; applied without balance it risks disintegration.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Decentralisation and Its Importance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 6.1 (source: lebs105.txt lines 1744-2042 (Decentralisation; centralisation and decentralisation as relative terms; importance i to vi))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Delegation versus Decentralisation' refers to.
questions.a: Delegation is the compulsory, day-to-day act of a superior passing authority to an immediate subordinate to lighten his own burden, while decentralisation is an optional top-management policy that extends delegation to the lowest levels to widen subordinates' autonomy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Delegation versus Decentralisation'.
questions.a: Compare on five bases -- nature (compulsory act versus optional policy), freedom of action, status (process versus result of policy), scope (narrow, two persons versus organisation-wide), purpose (relief of the manager versus enlarged role of subordinates).

questions.q: Under which section is 'Delegation versus Decentralisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 6.1 (source: lebs105.txt lines 2070-2123 (Delegation and Decentralisation comparative view))
